chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the one who is unconscious for a month: what does he make up of the prayer? He said: 'He makes up all of it, for the matter of prayer is severe/difficult.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up prayers after a long period of unconsciousness?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify the fiqh of *gha’ib al-salah* (missed prayers) for those in a prolonged coma. The Imam’s assertion that the 'matter of prayer is severe' (*shadid*) underscores the strictness of the obligation, distinguishing it from fasting where partial exemptions or different calculation methods might apply. This ruling emphasizes that the continuity of the divine command remains unbroken by unconsciousness, requiring full restitution of the missed units.
